literal: Song Yin, Xu Yan, Diao Yong, Xin Shaoxian, Wei Lang, Du Quan
idiomatic: Song Yin, Xu Yan, Diao Yong, Xin Shaoxian, Wei Lang, and Du Quan

literal: Biographies 14: Song Yin
idiomatic: Biographies 14: Song Yin

literal: 〈（Nephew Yin）〉
idiomatic: 〈（Nephew Yin）〉

literal: Yin
idiomatic: Yin

literal: 〈（Grandson Bian; Bian's grandson Qindao; Bian's clansman cousin Fan; Fan's disciple Shiliang）〉
idiomatic: 〈（Grandson Bian; Bian's grandson Qindao; Bian's clansman cousin Fan; Fan's disciple Shiliang）〉

literal: Shigui, Fan's brother Shijing, Xu Yan
idiomatic: Shigui, Fan's brother Shijing, and Xu Yan

literal: （Fifth-generation descendant Dun, Diao Yong
idiomatic: （Fifth-generation descendant Dun; Diao Yong

literal: （Son Zun; great-great-grandson Chongrou; Xin Shaoxian; Wei Lang; grandson Zican）
idiomatic: （Son Zun; great-great-grandson Chongrou; Xin Shaoxian; Wei Lang; grandson Zican）

literal: Song Yin, style Chumo, was a native of Jiexiu in Xihe.
idiomatic: Song Yin, whose style was Chumo, came from Jiexiu in Xihe.

literal: His great-grandfather was Shuang; his grandfather Huo; his father Gong.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather was Shuang, his grandfather Huo, and his father Gong.

literal: For generations they served the Murong clan, all holding prominent posts.
idiomatic: For generations the family served the Murong, every man reaching conspicuous rank.

literal: When Murong Jun moved the capital to Ye, Gong first established the household at Lieren in Guangping.
idiomatic: When Murong Jun moved the capital to Ye, Gong first settled the clan at Lieren in Guangping.

literal: Yin was supremely filial by nature and devoted himself to learning.
idiomatic: Yin was profoundly filial by nature and threw himself into study.

literal: He served Murong Chui as Recorder of the native prefecture.
idiomatic: He served Murong Chui as Recorder of the native prefecture.

literal: When Emperor Daowu pacified Zhongshan, Yin was appointed Director of the Ministry of Personnel in the Secretariat; over time he was promoted to Right Vice-Director of the mobile office, in charge of selection.
idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu pacified Zhongshan, Yin was made Director of the Ministry of Personnel in the Secretariat, then promoted over time to Right Vice-Director of the mobile office with charge of selection.

literal: He begged to retire on grounds of age and illness but was not permitted.
idiomatic: He asked to retire on grounds of age and illness and was refused.

literal: Soon he returned to Lieren for his mother's mourning; after the burial he was summoned back, so he abandoned wife and children and hid in Changle, and died there several years later.
idiomatic: He soon went home to Lieren for his mother's mourning; after the burial he was summoned again, abandoned wife and children, hid in Changle, and died there several years later.

literal: On his deathbed he told his son Jing: "If you can treat your father and elders with obedience at home and show fraternal duty in the community abroad, and if in office in the commandery you are fortunate enough to reach the post of Merit Officer Recorder, and serve with loyalty and integrity, that is enough.
idiomatic: On his deathbed he told his son Jing: "If you can obey father and elders at home and show fraternal duty abroad, and in commandery service are lucky enough to become Merit Officer Recorder and serve with loyalty and integrity, that is enough.

literal: Do not trouble yourself to go far to the central offices—for fear you cannot attain wealth and honor, you would only prolong the family's ruin."
idiomatic: Do not trouble yourself to reach the central offices—you may fail to grow rich and will only heap ruin on the household."

literal: If you forget my words, you will have wronged your father in death.
idiomatic: If you forget my words, you wrong your dead father.

literal: If ghosts have awareness, I will not return to eat with you."
idiomatic: If ghosts have awareness, I will not return to share your food."

literal: Yin's younger brother Xuan, style Daomao, together with Lu Xuan of Fanyang, Gao Yun of Bohai, Cui Jian of Boling, and his nephew Yin were all summoned and appointed as academicians in the Secretariat.
idiomatic: Yin's younger brother Xuan, style Daomao, was summoned along with Lu Xuan of Fanyang, Gao Yun of Bohai, Cui Jian of Boling, and his nephew Yin and appointed Secretariat academicians.

literal: Later he was made Vice-Director and Acting Commandant-Validator of the Ministry of Education.
idiomatic: He was later made Vice-Director and Acting Commandant-Validator of the Ministry of Education.

literal: He died; his posthumous title was Marquis Jian.
idiomatic: On his death he received the posthumous title Marquis Jian.

literal: Xuan's son Mo, style Qianren, inherited the title and died as Governor of Liaoxi.
idiomatic: Xuan's son Mo, style Qianren, inherited the title and died as Governor of Liaoxi.

literal: His son Luan inherited the title and served as Governor of Dongguan.
idiomatic: His son Luan inherited the title and held the post of Governor of Dongguan.

literal: Luan's younger brother Qiong, style Puxian, was famed for filial piety.
idiomatic: Luan's younger brother Qiong, style Puxian, was known for filial piety.

literal: When his mother had once been ill, in late autumn she longed for melons.
idiomatic: Once when his mother was ill, in late autumn she craved melons.

literal: Qiong dreamed he saw them, sought them, and obtained them; people at the time marveled.
idiomatic: Qiong dreamed of them, sought them, and found them; people at the time took it as a marvel.

literal: He died at home.
idiomatic: He died at home.

literal: Yin successively held the posts of Secretariat academician and Supernumerary Palace Attendant and was sent on a mission to the south.
idiomatic: Yin served as Secretariat academician and Supernumerary Palace Attendant and was sent on a mission south of the Yangtze.

literal: His title was Baron of Lieren.
idiomatic: He held the title Baron of Lieren.

literal: He died as Governor of Guangping.
idiomatic: He died as Governor of Guangping.

literal: His eldest son Xian inherited the title.
idiomatic: His eldest son Xian inherited the title.

literal: Xian had no sons and adopted his younger brother's son Bian as heir.
idiomatic: Xian had no sons and adopted his younger brother's son Bian as heir.

literal: Bian, style Yihe.
idiomatic: Bian, whose style was Yihe.

literal: His father Shuzhen married a sister of Li Fu of Zhao commandery and died because of the Fu affair.
idiomatic: His father Shuzhen had married a sister of Li Fu of Zhao commandery and died in the affair involving Fu.

literal: When Bian reached the capital he met Li Chong, Director of the Secretariat; their discussion lasted a full day.
idiomatic: When Bian reached the capital he met Li Chong, Director of the Secretariat, and they talked the day away.

literal: Chong was struck by him and said on leaving: "This man advances a thousand li in a day—talent fit to assist a king."
idiomatic: Chong was impressed and said as he left: "This man covers a thousand li in a day—talent fit to assist a king."

literal: When Xian died, Bian inherited the title.
idiomatic: When Xian died, Bian inherited the title.

literal: Bian and Li Biao were from the same commandery and treated each other with mutual esteem.
idiomatic: Bian and Li Biao were fellow townsmen and held each other in mutual esteem.

literal: When Biao was Secretariat Director he asked that Bian be made Assistant Editor in the Historiography Office.
idiomatic: When Biao was Secretariat Director he had Bian appointed Assistant Editor in the Historiography Office.

literal: He was transferred to Director in the Palace Department of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Director in the Palace Department of the Secretariat.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen once, during an assembly, questioned him in turn on the way of government.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen once, during court assembly, questioned him in turn on governance.

literal: Bian was young and his office low; he answered from below; his voice was clear and bright and his bearing admirable.
idiomatic: Though young and low in rank, Bian answered from below in a clear, bright voice with admirable bearing.

literal: The emperor praised him at length.
idiomatic: The emperor praised him at length.

literal: Thereupon he won great favor; he was given the personal name Bian, taking the sense of Bian He presenting jade while the King of Chu did not know its worth.
idiomatic: Thereupon he won great favor; he was granted the personal name Bian, evoking Bian He presenting jade while the King of Chu failed to recognize its worth.

literal: He was promoted to Vice-Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Supernumerary Palace Attendant and sent on a mission to Qi.
idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice-Director of the Secretariat with concurrent Supernumerary Palace Attendant and sent on a mission to Qi.

literal: Xiao Ziliang, Minister of Education of Qi, Wang Rong, Secretariat Director, and others all praised him, saying his will and spirit were forthright though not equal to Li Biao's, while his tone and bearing were harmonious and elegant and his manner leisurely and deep, surpassing Biao's.
idiomatic: Qi's Minister of Education Xiao Ziliang, Secretariat Director Wang Rong, and others praised him, saying his will and spirit were forthright though not equal to Li Biao's, while his tone and bearing were harmonious and elegant and his manner leisurely and deep—surpassing Biao.

literal: He was transferred to Vice-Director of the Palace Attendants.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice-Director of the Palace Attendants.

literal: At that time the Palace Attendant post ranked above the Secretariat.
idiomatic: At that time the Palace Attendant post ranked above the Secretariat.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen once discussed affairs south of the Yangtze and asked Bian about the number of years until the southern dynasty's fall.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen once discussed the south and asked Bian how long until the southern dynasty fell.

literal: Bian held that the Xiao father and son had done the realm no great service; having seized power by rebellion, they could not preserve it by obedience, and would surely fail to secure their descendants or hold the southern sea.
idiomatic: Bian held that the Xiao father and son had done the realm no great service; having seized power by rebellion they could not preserve it by obedience, and would surely fail to secure their descendants or hold the southern sea.

literal: If creatures feared their might, they might escape with their lives—that was all.
idiomatic: If others feared their might, they themselves might escape with their lives—that was all.

literal: Later, when the imperial carriage campaigned south, Bian was made Acting Vice-Commander of the Ministry of Education and Eastern-route deputy commander.
idiomatic: Later, when the emperor campaigned south, Bian was made Acting Vice-Commander of the Ministry of Education and Eastern-route deputy commander.

literal: When a soldier stole horse hobbles, he beheaded him and displayed the corpse; the three armies were awed and none dared break the law.
idiomatic: When a soldier stole horse hobbles, he beheaded him and displayed the corpse; the three armies were awed and none dared violate the law.

literal: Yellow Gate Gentleman Cui Guang recommended Bian to replace himself; the emperor did not agree but also rewarded Guang for knowing men.
idiomatic: Yellow Gate Gentleman Cui Guang recommended Bian to replace himself; the emperor refused but also praised Guang for knowing men.

literal: Before long Bian was made concurrent Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education.
idiomatic: Before long Bian was made concurrent Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education.

literal: At that time a great selection was made of officials within and without; the gentry of the four seas were all ranked; Bian alone handled the weighing of qualifications, and matters mostly pleased the emperor.
idiomatic: At that time officials within and without were selected in a great ranking of gentry throughout the realm; Bian alone handled the weighing of qualifications, and matters mostly pleased the emperor.

literal: Yet he loved to speak of people's hidden faults.
idiomatic: Yet he loved to speak of people's hidden faults.

literal: For great houses and clans he found inconvenient, he slandered them; for old families fallen into obscurity whose people were not to be feared, he spoke up for them.
idiomatic: For great houses he disliked he spread slander; for old families fallen into obscurity whose people were not to be feared, he spoke up for them.

literal: Bian also served as Grand Rectifier of his native commandery and demoted many surnames and clans, winning much resentment.
idiomatic: Bian also served as Grand Rectifier of his native commandery and demoted many clans, winning much resentment.

literal: He was promoted to Regular Palace Attendant, then soon to Right Guard General with concurrent charge of the Yellow Gate.
idiomatic: He was promoted to Regular Palace Attendant, then soon to Right Guard General with concurrent charge of the Yellow Gate.

literal: Bian repeatedly declined; the emperor said: "I know you as a friend—you must not refuse.
idiomatic: Bian repeatedly declined; the emperor said: "I know you as a friend—you must not refuse.

literal: How can you hold to a single office and not help me govern!
idiomatic: How can you cling to one office and not help me govern!

literal: The Regular Attendant post is a rough, subordinate place in the Yellow Gate;
idiomatic: Regular Attendant is a rough, subordinate post in the Yellow Gate;

literal: commanding the guards is a provisional assignment among the three guards—there is no room for empty modesty and abandoning a great commission."
idiomatic: commanding the guards is a provisional assignment among the three guards—there is no room for empty modesty and abandoning a great commission."

literal: Such was the favor he enjoyed.
idiomatic: Such was the favor he enjoyed.

literal: In the selection for the northern capital, Li Chong took much part and greatly suppressed the Song clan.
idiomatic: In the selection for the northern capital, Li Chong took much part and greatly suppressed the Song clan.

literal: Bian resented Chong and bonded with Li Biao in deep mutual esteem.
idiomatic: Bian resented Chong and bonded with Li Biao in deep mutual esteem.

literal: When Biao resisted Chong, Chong said to Biao: "You are like a dog!
idiomatic: When Biao resisted Chong, Chong said to Biao: "You are like a dog!

literal: Driven by someone else's hand."
idiomatic: Driven by someone else's hand."

literal: When Chong impeached Biao, he did not suffer the gravest penalty—Bian's doing.
idiomatic: When Chong impeached Biao, he did not suffer the gravest penalty—thanks to Bian.

literal: When Biao was stripped of his name, Bian sighed greatly and secretly plotted his restoration.
idiomatic: When Biao was stripped of his name, Bian sighed greatly and secretly plotted his restoration.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowen fell ill at Runan and grew gravely ill, for more than ten days he did not see attending ministers; only Prince of Pengcheng Xie and a few others were at his side.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen fell ill at Runan and grew gravely ill, for more than ten days he saw no attending ministers; only Prince of Pengcheng Xie and a few others were at his side.

literal: When he improved slightly he summoned the Gentlemen of the Gate and the elders of the imperial clan.
idiomatic: When he improved slightly he summoned the Gentlemen of the Gate and the elders of the imperial clan.

literal: Those who entered could not all weep; only Bian and Acting Vice-Commander of the Ministry of Education Zhang Hai sobbed and shed tears, and the emperor valued him all the more.
idiomatic: Those who entered could not all weep; only Bian and Acting Vice-Commander Zhang Hai sobbed and shed tears, and the emperor valued him all the more.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned to Maquan, Bian was left in his original post with concurrent Minister of Sacrifices, in charge of the seven military offices.
idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned to Maquan, Bian was left in his original post with concurrent Minister of Sacrifices, in charge of the seven military offices.

literal: On departure the emperor took his hand and said: "The great affairs of state lie in sacrifice and war; therefore I put you in charge of both offices."
idiomatic: On departure the emperor took his hand and said: "The great affairs of state lie in sacrifice and war; therefore I put you in charge of both offices."

literal: Bian bowed his head and declined with thanks.
idiomatic: Bian bowed his head and declined with thanks.

literal: Bian toiled at the king's business and enjoyed favor second only to Li Chong.
idiomatic: Bian toiled at the king's business and enjoyed favor second only to Li Chong.

literal: The emperor often said Bian could serve as Director of the Ministry of Personnel; when he died, the testamentary edict appointed Bian to that post.
idiomatic: The emperor often said Bian could serve as Director of the Ministry of Personnel; when he died, the testamentary edict appointed Bian to that post.

literal: He was one of six, with Prince of Xianyang Xi and others, who were to assist the government, but Bian died first.
idiomatic: He was one of six, with Prince of Xianyang Xi and others, who were to assist the government, but Bian died first.

literal: He was thirty-eight.
idiomatic: He was thirty-eight.

literal: He was posthumously made Governor of Yingzhou; his posthumous title was Zhenshun.
idiomatic: He was posthumously made Governor of Yingzhou; his posthumous title was Zhenshun.

literal: Bian was fond of boasting by nature and considered himself of the finest blood.
idiomatic: Bian was fond of boasting by nature and considered himself of the finest blood.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen, because Guo Zuo was a famous house of Jin and Wei, said casually to Bian: "You ought to yield place to the house of Guo Zuo."
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen, because Guo Zuo was a famous house of Jin and Wei, said casually to Bian: "You ought to yield place to the house of Guo Zuo."

literal: Bian smiled and said: "My house is not willing to yield to Zuo."
idiomatic: Bian smiled and said: "My house is not willing to yield to Zuo."

literal: The emperor said: "From Han and Wei onward your house has had neither high office nor outstanding talent—how can you not yield?"
idiomatic: The emperor said: "From Han and Wei onward your house has had neither high office nor outstanding talent—how can you not yield?"

literal: Bian said: "I stand on my own integrity and clarity; in any case I will not yield."
idiomatic: Bian said: "I stand on my own integrity and clarity; in any case I will not yield."

literal: After the attendants left, the emperor said to Prince of Pengcheng Xie: "Bian's person is not bad, yet he still wants to boast of his house—it is very strange."
idiomatic: After the attendants left, the emperor said to Prince of Pengcheng Xie: "Bian's person is not bad, yet he still wants to boast of his house—it is very strange."

literal: His eldest son Wei, style Boxu, inherited his father's title.
idiomatic: His eldest son Wei, style Boxu, inherited his father's title.

literal: He served as Attendant of the Inner Palace.
idiomatic: He served as Attendant of the Inner Palace.

literal: For fawning on Gao Zhao he was sent out as Chief Clerk of the Dragon-Charger Office in Yizhou; he pleaded illness and did not go.
idiomatic: For fawning on Gao Zhao he was sent out as Chief Clerk of the Dragon-Charger Office in Yizhou; he pleaded illness and did not go.

literal: When Grand Commandant Prince of Qinghe Yi assisted the government, because Wei was a famous minister's son he recommended him as Direct Transmission Gentleman and recruited his younger brother Ji as Retainer.
idiomatic: When Grand Commandant Prince of Qinghe Yi assisted the government, because Wei was a famous minister's son he recommended him as Direct Transmission Gentleman and recruited his younger brother Ji as Retainer.

literal: When Empress Dowager Ling took power she entrusted Yuan Cha, who grew arrogant with favor; Yi often judged him by public principle.
idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling took power she entrusted Yuan Cha, who grew arrogant with favor; Yi often judged him by public principle.

literal: Cha hated him greatly and plotted to harm Yi; he joined with Wei in a plan and promised him wealth and honor.
idiomatic: Cha hated him greatly and plotted to harm Yi; he joined with Wei in a plan and promised him wealth and honor.

literal: Wei saw Cha's power and favor growing daily and reported to Director of the Dye Works Han Wenshu and his son that they plotted rebellion to install Yi.
idiomatic: Wei saw Cha's power and favor growing daily and reported to Director of the Dye Works Han Wenshu and his son that they plotted rebellion to install Yi.

literal: Yi was taken and held in the inner palace.
idiomatic: Yi was taken and held in the inner palace.

literal: Wenshu and his son, in fear, fled.
idiomatic: Wenshu and his son, in fear, fled.
